one_liner: Code hosting, version control, pull requests, issues and CI/CD for software teams.
auth_notes: REST auth via fine-grained PAT (recommended over classic), classic PAT, GitHub App tokens (JWT for app auth, installation and user-to-server tokens), or OAuth app tokens. GitHub recommends GitHub Apps over OAuth apps. Basic auth only for some app endpoints (client_id:client_secret); username/password is not supported. Token sent as 'Authorization: Bearer' (or 'token'). SAML-SSO orgs require authorizing classic PATs.
access_notes: Any GitHub account can create PATs and register OAuth/GitHub Apps. Rate limits: 60 req/h unauthenticated, 5,000 req/h per user for PAT/OAuth, GitHub App installations at least 5,000 (up to 12,500; 15,000 on Enterprise Cloud).
api_breadth_notes: Very large REST surface (repos, issues, PRs, actions, orgs, teams, checks, packages, security, etc.) plus a GraphQL API; hundreds of operations.
mcp_notes: github/github-mcp-server ('GitHub's official MCP Server'). Remote hosted at https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/ (OAuth or PAT bearer); local via Docker image ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server or binary (stdio). 23 toolsets local, 25 remote.
notes: Webhooks can be created at repo, org, GitHub App, Marketplace and Sponsors levels (docs.github.com/en/webhooks/about-webhooks). No dedicated sandbox environment; free accounts/orgs are used for testing. Repeated invalid-credential requests trigger temporary 403 lockouts. GitHub App installation tokens get higher rate limits than user tokens.

one_liner: Frontend cloud platform for deploying, hosting and scaling web apps and serverless functions.
auth_notes: REST API uses access tokens created on the Account Tokens page, sent as 'Authorization: Bearer'. Tokens can be scoped to Full Account, Team, or a single Project; full-account tokens need teamId/slug to target non-default teams. OAuth exists via 'Sign in with Vercel' (GA; 1h access token, 30-day rotating refresh token) but its API/team-resource permissions are 'currently in private beta'. Marketplace integrations receive bearer tokens on install and can use OAuth2.
access_notes: Getting-started guide requires only a Vercel account to create a token; no plan gate stated for the REST API. Account-level webhooks are Pro/Enterprise only. Sign in with Vercel API permissions are private beta.
api_breadth_notes: REST reference lists ~474 operations across ~45 groups (projects, deployments, domains, DNS, env vars, teams, logs, drains, feature flags, firewall/security, AI Gateway, sandboxes, webhooks, integrations, billing). OpenAPI at vercel.com/openapi.json; TypeScript SDK @vercel/sdk.
mcp_notes: Vercel MCP, remote at https://mcp.vercel.com with OAuth (Streamable HTTP). Available on all plans. Only reviewed/approved clients or clients using CIMD (Client ID Metadata Document) can connect. Tools: docs search, projects/deployments, deployment logs, Web Analytics.
notes: For an end-user OAuth toolkit, Sign in with Vercel API permissions are private beta, so token-based auth (or a Vercel Integration) is the practical path today. Account webhooks (deployment/project/flag/firewall events, x-vercel-signature) need Pro/Enterprise (docs /docs/webhooks); integration webhooks are separate. 'Sandboxes' in the API is a compute product, not a test environment. Pricing page not fetched; Hobby free status assumed from token flow needing only an account.

one_liner: Web hosting and deployment platform for sites, serverless functions, forms and edge.
auth_notes: OAuth2 applications (client key/secret registered at app.netlify.com/applications; authorize at https://app.netlify.com/authorize) for public integrations, or personal access tokens as Bearer. SAML SSO teams deny PAT team access by default unless opted in. Password reset invalidates existing PATs and OAuth tokens.
access_notes: Free plan ($0 forever, 300 credits) includes 'Deploy from AI, Git, or API'. No API plan gating described. Rate limit 500 req/min; API deploys limited to 3/min and 100/day; higher limits via support.
api_breadth_notes: OpenAPI spec (github.com/netlify/open-api swagger.yml) has ~188 operationIds: sites, deploys, builds, env vars, files, forms/submissions, hooks, DNS, accounts/members, functions, snippets, SSL.
mcp_notes: Netlify MCP server: remote at https://mcp.netlify.com/mcp (recommended) and local package @netlify/mcp; source github.com/netlify/netlify-mcp. Auth mechanism not specified on docs page (agents get a Netlify login link).
notes: Outgoing hooks (webhook/email/Slack deploy notifications) are an API resource group. Pagination via Link header, max per_page 100. Deploys use file-digest or ZIP upload. Go and JS clients available. Strict deploy rate limits matter for agent-driven deploy tools.

one_liner: Connectivity cloud: CDN, DNS, security, Zero Trust and Workers developer platform.
auth_notes: Scoped API tokens (user tokens under My Profile, or account-owned tokens with an endpoint compatibility matrix) sent as Bearer; legacy Global API Key + email still required by a few endpoints. Self-managed OAuth clients (changelog 2026-06-03): Authorization Code only (PKCE S256 for public clients), scopes mirror API token permissions; clients start private (own account only) and become public after DNS TXT domain verification.
access_notes: Any account can create API tokens; no plan requirement stated. Free usage tiers exist across products. OAuth client creation needs Super Admin/Admin/OAuth Client Write role; going public requires name, logo, URL, scopes and domain verification (no separate review described).
api_breadth_notes: 2,500+ endpoints (per Cloudflare API MCP server docs) across accounts, zones, DNS, cache, SSL, firewall/WAF, Workers, R2, D1, KV, email, analytics, Zero Trust, etc. SDKs: TypeScript, Python, Go, Terraform.
mcp_notes: Cloudflare API MCP server at https://mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp (remote, OAuth or API token bearer), code-mode with search()/execute()/docs() covering whole API. Plus product servers (docs, containers, browser, DEX, CASB, agents).
notes: Notifications can be delivered to generic webhooks on all plans (up to 100 destinations without a paid zone; developers.cloudflare.com/notifications/get-started/configure-webhooks/). Public OAuth is new (mid-2026); making a client public is irreversible. Some Organization endpoints still require Global API key + email. Token secrets shown once.

one_liner: Open-source Postgres backend platform with auth, storage, realtime and edge functions.
auth_notes: Management API: personal access tokens (scoped PATs recommended; legacy PATs have full user privileges) or OAuth2 apps (authorize at api.supabase.com/v1/oauth/authorize, PKCE recommended, scopes fixed at app creation, token exchange with Basic client auth, refresh supported). Project data APIs use per-project keys.
access_notes: Free plan $0 with 2 active projects (pause after 1 week inactivity), unlimited API requests. OAuth apps registered self-serve from org settings > OAuth Apps; no review step described. Branching is paid-only.
api_breadth_notes: Management API groups: advisors, analytics, auth config, billing, compute, database, domains, edge functions, environments/branches, OAuth, organizations, projects, realtime, rest, secrets, storage, webhooks. Rate limit 120 req/min per user/scope/endpoint.
mcp_notes: Hosted at https://mcp.supabase.com/mcp with OAuth dynamic client registration (PAT header for CI). Tool groups: database, debugging, development, edge functions, account, docs, branching (paid), storage (off by default). Supports ?read_only=true and ?project_ref= scoping. Local CLI server at localhost:54321/mcp.
notes: Management API includes organization and project webhooks; database webhooks also exist. 'Sandbox' = local CLI stack and paid branching, not a hosted sandbox. Supabase warns its MCP runs with developer permissions and is exposed to prompt injection via DB data; prefer read-only and project scoping. Some endpoints have stricter limits (log queries 30/min).

one_liner: Graph database (AuraDB cloud or self-managed) queried with the Cypher language.
auth_notes: Query API (Cypher over HTTP, /db/<database>/query/v2): Basic (DB username/password) or Bearer token from an SSO provider (server must be SSO-configured). Aura management API: OAuth2 client credentials (client ID/secret from Account Settings exchanged at api.neo4j.io/oauth/token; 1h tokens).
access_notes: Aura docs: 'All tiers can create Aura API credentials'; AuraDB Free exists (rate limit 25 req/min for Free/Pro-trial vs 125 for paid). Self-managed Neo4j also exposes the Query API (5.19+).
api_breadth_notes: Query API is a small set of endpoints but executes arbitrary Cypher; Aura API manages instances and related resources. Exact Aura API operation count not verified (spec page failed to load).
mcp_notes: github.com/neo4j/mcp ('Neo4j official MCP Server'), pip neo4j-mcp-server / Docker mcp/neo4j; local STDIO with DB user/password env vars. Tools: get-schema, read-cypher, write-cypher, list-gds-procedures; read-only mode. Docs at neo4j.com/docs/mcp. No hosted server found. neo4j-contrib/mcp-neo4j is Labs/community.
blocker: Per-instance connection URI and database credentials required
notes: Database toolkit: each user supplies instance host + DB user/password (no end-user OAuth for data plane unless their server is SSO-configured). Aura management uses separate client credentials. Fetch failures: neo4j.com/docs/aura/api/specification/ (404) and /docs/aura/platform/api/specification/ (empty). Sandbox = AuraDB Free / Neo4j Desktop / self-managed, per MCP docs prerequisites.

one_liner: Cloud data warehouse/AI data platform for SQL analytics, data sharing and Cortex AI.
auth_notes: SQL API/REST APIs accept Snowflake OAuth or External OAuth (Bearer), key-pair JWT (max 1h), programmatic access tokens (token-type header PROGRAMMATIC_ACCESS_TOKEN), and workload identity federation. Snowflake OAuth supports authorization_code + refresh_token; custom clients are configured via a security integration in each account. ACCOUNTADMIN/SECURITYADMIN etc. are blocked from OAuth by default.
access_notes: Self-service trial: 30 days or until free usage balance is exhausted; email-only signup, card needed for AI features and to continue. After trial the account is suspended until upgraded. No permanent free tier found.
api_breadth_notes: SQL API (run any SQL) plus GA Snowflake REST APIs covering ~41 resource types in 15 categories (users/roles/grants, warehouses, databases/schemas/tables, stages/pipes, tasks/streams, services, Cortex Search/Inference, alerts, etc.).
mcp_notes: Snowflake-managed MCP server hosted inside the customer account (CREATE MCP SERVER; URL https://<account_url>/api/v2/databases/{db}/schemas/{schema}/mcp-servers/{name}). Tools: Cortex Agent, Cortex Analyst, Cortex Search, SQL execution, custom UDF/procs; up to 50 tools. Snowflake OAuth (no dynamic client registration) or PAT. GA/preview status not stated.
blocker: Per-account OAuth security integration and account URL; trial-only
notes: Every tenant has its own account URL; OAuth requires the customer admin to create a security integration (custom-client setup page not fetched; per oauth-snowflake-overview pointer). PAT + account identifier is the simplest toolkit path. Webhook notification integrations only send to Slack, Teams, PagerDuty, Jira, ServiceNow (not arbitrary URLs). snowflake.com trial page and developer guide returned 403; trial credit amount ($400) seen only in search snippets, not verified.

one_liner: Managed cloud MongoDB document database service with search, vector search and streams.
auth_notes: Atlas Administration API: service accounts (OAuth 2.0 access tokens via client ID/secret, i.e. client credentials) or API keys using HTTP Digest auth. Both grantable at org or project level (Organization Owner/Project Owner). Delegated access via 'Atlas App Connections' exists for partner apps and MCP clients (off by default for existing orgs); no public third-party auth-code flow documented. Data plane uses driver connection strings.
access_notes: Free M0 tier is 'Free forever'; no plan/tier requirement stated for Admin API credentials. API reachable only over public internet; org IP access lists can block requests.
api_breadth_notes: Admin API v2 (https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2, date-versioned Accept header) covers orgs, projects, clusters, DB users, access lists, alerts, backups, search, streams, etc. Exact count not taken.
mcp_notes: MongoDB MCP Server (docs at mongodb.com/docs/mcp-server): local server plus an 'Atlas Managed MCP' option. ~54 tools: ~23 Atlas admin tools (need service account credentials), ~25 database tools, 4 Atlas Local (Docker) tools, 2 assistant tools. Hosted auth details not verified.
blocker: Data operations need driver connection; no REST data API
notes: Atlas Data API is not listed among current programmatic access tools (it was deprecated); CRUD/query tools must use drivers with a per-user connection string, while admin tools use the REST Admin API. Generic webhook integration for alert notifications exists (docs/atlas/tutorial/third-party-service-integrations). Sandbox = free M0 cluster or Atlas Local via Docker. Get-started MCP page fetch was truncated.

one_liner: Cloud monitoring and security platform for metrics, logs, traces, incidents and alerts.
auth_notes: REST API: API key (write) plus application key (read) headers; scoped application keys via service accounts recommended. Site-specific hosts (api.datadoghq.com, .eu, us3, us5, ap1, ap2, uk1, gov). OAuth2 (auth code + PKCE) is for API-based integrations built via the Developer Platform in a Datadog Partner Sandbox account. MCP also accepts personal/service access tokens as Bearer.
access_notes: Free Infrastructure tier (up to 5 Basic hosts, 1-day retention) and product free trials. Pricing page does not break down API access by plan. OAuth client creation tied to partner sandbox/integration publishing.
api_breadth_notes: v1/v2 REST APIs across metrics, monitors, dashboards, logs, events, incidents, synthetics, SLOs, security, users/roles, etc.; hundreds of operations (not counted).
mcp_notes: Remote Datadog MCP Server at https://mcp.datadoghq.com/v1/mcp (per-site variants; not on gov sites). OAuth 2.0 recommended; also PAT/SAT bearer or DD_API_KEY/DD_APPLICATION_KEY headers. Requires mcp_read/mcp_write permissions and org-level MCP access enabled by admin; some toolsets in Preview.
notes: Toolkit must capture the user's Datadog site to pick the base URL. API+app keys are self-serve; end-user OAuth requires building an integration through the Datadog partner Developer Platform (Partner Sandbox = the sandbox). Webhooks integration sends monitor/alert notifications to custom URLs with Basic/OAuth2 auth. MCP fair-use limit 50 tool calls per 10s.

one_liner: Application error tracking and performance monitoring for developers.
auth_notes: Bearer auth tokens from internal integrations, user auth tokens (Personal Tokens), or OAuth2 access tokens (authorization code + PKCE or device flow; expire after 30 days, refreshable). Public integrations get install-scoped tokens (8h expiry, JWT-bearer refresh). DSN auth only on some endpoints; legacy API keys via HTTP Basic.
access_notes: Pricing table shows 'API: No' and 'Third-party integrations: No' on the free Developer plan; Team and above include API. Business has a 14-day trial with no credit card. Public integrations start unpublished (own org only); publishing to all orgs requires Sentry review. Self-hosted Sentry is also supported.
api_breadth_notes: REST API covering organizations, projects, teams, issues/events, releases, alerts, monitors, replays, integrations, etc. (count not verified).
mcp_notes: Hosted at https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp (OAuth; org/project-scoped URLs). Local stdio via 'sentry mcp' (Sentry CLI login) or legacy npx @sentry/mcp-server; supports self-hosted Sentry.
blocker: API access requires Team plan after trial
notes: Pricing table claims no API on the free Developer plan; in practice user tokens may still work on free orgs, so verify with a live account. Integration platform sends webhooks (installation, issue, error, etc.). Where OAuth apps are registered for the generic OAuth2 flow was not verified; public integrations need review to publish. Self-hosted Sentry is a free test option.
